description.narrative: The project addresses the imperative to pursue the expansion of technical, occupational and vocational education, job generation, and social promotion. 1.3 Works Construction of the Vocational Training Center of Les Cayes is 100% complete and provisional acceptance of work took place on April 30, 2021. Considering all the actual and planned expenses, resources available on the hard component would be enough to build a second center. The 6th Project Steering Committee was held on July 1st 2021 and the decision to build, equip and put into operation two professional training centers, one in Les Cayes and the other in Fort Liberté was approved. The Steering Committee also approved the substantive revision to extend the project until December 31, 2022 in order to meet the June 30, 2023 closing deadline. By the end of the first semester of 2021, the HRF had extended the fund until June 30, 2023. Currently, there is a bidding process underway for the construction of the second VTC in Fort Liberté. Due to security constraints the third center at Saint Marc will no longer be built. The fundamental element is that the security situation is deteriorating in Haiti. The department of Artibonite where the city of Saint-Marc is located had become too insecure with the proliferation of gangs in this region (Savien gang) with its lot of kidnapping, rape and murder. It was impossible for the project team to go to this region or for the firms that will eventually have to build and supervise these works, hence the decision to concentrate on Fort-Liberté which to date is in a rather calm region. During the first semester of 2021, all project activities had been put on standby.
The bidding process to purchase equipment for the VTC of Les Cayes was launched several times but could not be concluded as there were no valid proposals. The strategy to purchase equipment for the VTC at Les Cayes was revised and will count with SENAI´s technical support to improve technical aspects and enable the conclusion of the purchasing process.
2.1, 2.2, 2.3 and 3.1 The soft component (training) strategy was designed to be implemented after the VTCs were built and fully equipped. Also, for the soft component implementation, the professional teams (managers and teachers) of the VTCs had to be identified and ready to receive the training sessions at new facilities. The construction delay prevented the implementation of this strategy, and due to the challenges imposed by the Covid-19 pandemic, the alternative was to develop online training courses which were fully implemented until 31 December 2020 for the Haitian professional teams. The proposal was approved at the Fifth Steering Committee Meeting, held on July 29, 2020. The activities included: - 1. Creation of a distance training platform in French for managers, instructors and administrative staff; - 2. Realization of a distance education module for managers, instructors and administrative staff, on pedagogical matters; - 3. Preparation of guidelines in 5 areas of professional training.
The INFP provided the physical structure to conduct the distance training courses and the project was responsible for the provision of internet connection and computer equipment. UNDP Brazil and SENAI signed a Letter of Agreement so that activities could be carried out.
The distance education activities for the group of 30 instructors took place from 22 November to 17 December, 2021.
With the authorization by the Haiti Reconstruction Fund of the project´s extension end date until 31st December 2022, the project board proposed the 6th Steering Committee Meeting which was held on 1st July 2021 to discuss the continuation of activities of the soft component, such as the distance training activities provided by SENAI, for the second semester of 2021 and first semester of 2022 and also the trainings in Brazil to be held in the first semester of 2022 for the managers and administrative staff and for the instructors. UNDP Brazil and SENAI signed a Letter of Agreement to continue the training activities. The distance training activities were provided by SENAI during the second semester of 2021 and in the first semester of 2022 training courses are to be held in Brazil for the managers and staff and for the instructors.
4. The VI Steering Committee Meeting was held on 1 July 2021 and the following decisions were made: i) The budget to complete the works of the Vocational Center at Les Cayes and also the Vocational Center at Fort Liberté, including the retaining wall, was approved. The Vocational Center of Saint Marc will no longer be built. The substantive revision will be approved to reflect the budget, including the transfer of the budget from the soft component to the hard component. ii) The substantive revision of the project will include budget for SENAI to act as an Implementing Agent in the amount of USD 2,421,551.73. iii) The continuation of the training activities proposed by SENAI was approved. An amendment to the current Letter of Agreement will be signed in order to reflect those activities. iv) The purchase of equipment for Fort Liberté and additional actions proposed by the INFP (small purchases, air conditioning, generator set, inverter, furniture, and equipment) was approved. v) The substantive revision of the project will be validated in letter form and the signatures collected electronically by the Docusign platform.
The Projects narrative report for the period of 1 January 2019 to 31 December 2021 was delivered to the MPTF Office.

4. The VII Steering Committee Meeting was held on April 29, 2022 and the following decisions were approved: i) The operational closure of the project will take place on September 30, 2022, and the final project closure will take place on December 31 2022; ii) The Vocational Training Center at Fort Liberté will no longer be built due to lack of funds, time constraints and security issues; iii) Some activities proposed for the “hard” component and the “soft” component at the VII Project Steering Committee Meeting were revised.
